preamble: Raising of /æ/ all the way to /i/ is rare and in the clearest case morphophonological. In Uyghur 'vowel reduction', the low vowels /ɑ æ/ are raised to [i] in word-medial open syllables created by suffixation (mewæ 'fruit' > mewisi 'its fruit'); underived roots and some loanwords resist it, and in rapid speech the raising can affect a word-final vowel before a following word.

examples.note: Stem-final /æ/ ends up in a word-medial open syllable after suffixation and raises to [i].
The same verb stem keeps /æ/ before the consonant-initial gerund suffix (closed syllable) but raises it before -di.

examples.from: [ɑdil hæsængæ bærdi] 'Adil gave it to Hesen'
examples.note: In rapid speech the word-final dative vowel /æ/ raises to [i] before the following word, extending the rule across the word boundary. Underived roots such as /mɑqɑlæ/ 'academic article' do not raise.

sources: Mayer, C., McCollum, A., & Eziz, G. (2022). Issues in Uyghur phonology. Language and Linguistics Compass 16(12), e12478. https://doi.org/10.1111/lnc3.12478

Mayer, C. (2023). Opacity in parallel models of phonology: Insights from Uyghur backness harmony (talk slides, CSU Fullerton). https://sites.socsci.uci.edu/~cjmayer/papers/cmayer_csuf_colloquium_may_2023.pdf
